evaluated.question: plugin/README.md makes factual claims your assumptions did not cover: `add_prompts` counts against the plan's prompt limit; `generate_article` spends content credits; Claude keeps the OAuth token and never sees the password; the skill is named `seerly`; the engine list (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews). For each, was it checked against code, tool descriptions or tools-list.json in the session (cite the entry), or written from earlier context without a check?
evaluated.answer:
General point: the README was written in one Write at entry 6229, right after the gap report at 6214. No command between them reads code or tool descriptions. So none of the five claims was re-checked at the moment of writing. Each one traces to something the session read earlier, except the engine list.

1. add_prompts counts against the plan's prompt limit
   - Not checked when writing.
   - Source in the session: the tool description in tools-list.json, dumped from the real backend server at 5692-5698. It was rendered into references and found identical to the plugin pages (5709: "0 differing lines").
   - The reference text, plugin/skills/seerly/references/add_prompts.md line 5: "Skips prompts already tracked and stops at the plan's prompt limit."
   - The 6134 script read tools-list.json, but it printed only the annotations.
   - Inference from code (airo-backend main, add-prompts.tool.ts):
     - lines 80-91: the limit is maxTotalPrompts minus tracked prompts;
     - lines 144-150: the save goes through the existing create_topic_with_prompts route.
     - So 'counts against' is consistent with 'stops at'.
   - Caveat from the plan doc line 201: "add_prompts previews against the live count; the save can still return 402 if the stored counter is higher."
2. generate_article spends content credits
   - Not checked when writing.
   - Same source: references/generate_article.md line 5, "Spends content credits. Call it first without confirm: it returns the credit cost and the credits left."
   - SKILL.md line 60 says the same. The session read SKILL.md in full at 5629/5640; at 5796: "I read the skill, the manifests and the scripts in full".
   - It matches the consent-copy fix earlier in the session (C17): "generate articles (which use your credits)".
3. Claude keeps the OAuth token and never sees the password
   - Not checked against code when writing. It rests on the session's own runs of the flow:
     - local SDK OAuth flow, 27/27 (5430);
     - prod `claude mcp login "plugin:seerly:seerly"` (6042);
     - 6108: "Claude Code registered itself, sent you to seerly.app to sign in and approve, and got its token through the localhost callback."
   - Sign-in and consent happen on seerly.app (/login, /connect), never in the client.
   - Only Claude Code was exercised. claude.ai, where Anthropic's servers hold the token, was not tested; that test was asked of the user.
   - Inference from code: seerly-front app/login/page.tsx has password fields (6 matches), so password login exists. The claim holds because entry happens on seerly.app.
   - The README does not mention that the token is the 7-day login JWT with no disconnect, which is an open item in the plan doc.
4. The skill is named `seerly`
   - Checked in the session:
     - 5629/5640 `cat plugin/skills/seerly/SKILL.md`;
     - 5854, the install from the public repo showed "one skill and one MCP server";
     - 6108: "Claude used the plugin's `seerly` skill".
   - Code: SKILL.md line 2 is `name: seerly`.
5. Engine list (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews)
   - Never checked against code in the session. It was copied from existing repo text that already said the same: root README line 3 (in base 3e1d39f), plugin/plugin.json longDescription line 18, SKILL.md description line 3.
   - Inference from code, found while answering this and NOT in the session: airo-backend src/config/llm-models.config.ts lines 556-566. On the claude entry: "NOT RUNNING IN PRODUCTION as of 2026-08-30: the prod backend sets DISABLED_PROVIDERS=claude, and ProviderConfigAdapterService.applyGlobalDisabled (provider-config-adapter.service.ts:91) filters claude out of the engine list."
   - So 'Seerly measures how ... Claude ... mention' may be untrue in prod today. This is a code comment, and the gate is an env var; I did not check the prod env.
   - If true, the same overclaim is in the pre-existing manifest and skill text, and it would reach the public listing.
   - I could not put this to the developer: there is no ask tool in this role's access.
